privacy.title: What we store
privacy.intro: This page says what the builder stores today and what it does not. If something changes, we change this page.
privacy.name: Your name, as you give it. Whoever leads a campaign you play in sees it.
privacy.email: Your email address, if you give one. We only send it the link to get back in if you lose your password, and only when you ask for it. Nobody else sees it.
privacy.password: Your passwords, only as a check value, with the name you give them. Nobody can work out a password from it.
privacy.keys: Your access keys, if you make any: only as a check value, with the name you give it and the date. We do not record when a key is used.
privacy.campaigns: Your campaigns: their name and who leads them.
privacy.cookies: One cookie so you stay logged in. And one that remembers your language before you log in.
privacy.notStored: What we do not do today
privacy.noTracking: No ads, no recording of your clicks, no statistics about you as a person. The operator sees only totals: how many accounts and characters there are.
privacy.noThirdParty: Your browser loads nothing from other sites. No outside fonts, no outside scripts.
privacy.live: Whoever has a character open sees who else has it open: the name, and whether in the browser or with a program. A change to the character shows the other person who made it, by name. The server only knows this while you are connected. It writes it down nowhere.
privacy.admin: The operator sees how many people are logged in right now. Not who. This is stored nowhere.
privacy.languageModel: A language model of your choice can read your characters and build with you: through the address /mcp of this server, or with a program you download. Both need an access key you make yourself. Today our server has no language model in it and passes your characters on to nobody. They go only to the language model you set up yourself.
privacy.delete: You can delete your account in the settings at any time. Then everything is gone; only feedback you sent stays, without the account.

mcp.title: Build with a language model
mcp.intro: A language model can read your characters and build with you. You write to it what you want. It asks the character builder and puts in your choices.
mcp.choose: You choose the language model yourself. The data it reads goes there.
mcp.what: MCP is a shared language that programs use to give a language model tools. Many programs with a language model know it.
mcp.addressText: You put this address into your program.
mcp.keyText: Your program needs an access key. With it, it gets into your account, and only yours. You make it in the settings.
mcp.keyLogin: Log in first to do this.
mcp.programsText: Everywhere, put your key in place of {key}.
mcp.claudeCodeText: Type this command in the terminal, the window for commands:
mcp.cursorText: In Cursor, open the settings and then MCP. Add a new server. Cursor then opens the file mcp.json. Put this in:
mcp.openWebUiText: As admin: open the settings and then the external tools. Add a server. As the type, choose MCP over HTTP. Put in the address above. As the login, choose Bearer and put in your key.
mcp.otherText: Programs that know MCP over HTTP need two things: the address above and this header line.
mcp.otherApi: Without MCP, a program can also use the API directly. All of it is on the page
mcp.localText: Some programs only start servers on your own computer, for example Claude Desktop. For those, take the package below. The guide inside leads you step by step.
mcp.selfText: The package is a small program. It runs in two ways:
mcp.selfPrivate: With your key, it runs privately on your own computer, only for you.
mcp.selfPublic: Without a key, it runs publicly as a server over HTTP. Then each request brings its own key.
mcp.selfForeign: If you use someone else's server of this kind, you give your key to whoever runs it.
mcp.privacyText: Today our server has no language model in it and passes your characters on to nobody. They go only to the language model you set up yourself.
mcp.privacyKey: The key is a password. If in doubt, withdraw it.
